title: Private-coin complexity at most deterministic complexity
statement:
Let $f : X \times Y \to \alpha$ be a function of two arguments, and let $\varepsilon \ge 0$ be an error parameter. Then the $\varepsilon$-error private-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ is at most its deterministic communication complexity:
\[
  R_\varepsilon(f) \;\le\; D(f),
\]
as an inequality of extended natural numbers.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → α is a two-argument function
replaced:
For any function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ and any error parameter $\varepsilon \ge 0$,
the private-coin communication complexity satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{CC}_{\mathrm{priv}}(f, \varepsilon) \;\le\; \mathrm{CC}_{\mathrm{det}}(f).
\]
The inequality holds because every deterministic protocol can be viewed as a
private-coin protocol with zero error by embedding it via \texttt{toPrivateCoin}.
